Part 3 starts with data management, the work between the raw survey files and the panel that you used in the morning: the steps of the build, what may be shared at each of them, and the checks that a build from many files needs. Then comes the task that the R work of the day leads up to, in which you reproduce, to the third decimal, the result that Multi100 recorded for one of three analysts, chosen by you. The part ends on what the reproduction took, and on the slips in the code that the analysts deposited. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. Data management

**On the slides.** The slides go from sixteen Eurobarometer files to one panel, and say who may see each step of the build. The slides then show the codebook that sits beside every file, and the checks on the inputs that a build from many files needs.

To go further: [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd).

## 2. Hands-on 3a – Checking a panel

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

In an editable cell of the browser lab, or in the working script of the workspace, count the respondents behind each year of the panel. Then find the rows of `analyst_KQXUE.csv` in which a wave is counted twice, and the rows of `analyst_018OL.csv` in which a wave carries the wrong year. Say in one sentence what each file reveals, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. The [codebook of the two files](../../cases/eu-frames/data/analyst_panels_codebook.md) explains their columns.

## 3. The instruction of Multi100

**On the slides.** The slides read the four instructions of the second Multi100 task and say what each of them assumes. The slides then show the columns of the panel and the three analyses that can be reproduced on aggregate data.

## 4. Task 3 – The reproduction

[Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Choose one analyst and fill the gaps in its cell, which has a hint and a full solution under it. In the working script of the workspace the three analyses are written out. The first run of the cell of 018OL downloads two packages, about 32 MB. Type the analyst and the value in the chat, for example `C6HJR t = -3.804`, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go.

| Analyst | Data | Model | Recorded by Multi100 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C6HJR | the course panel, `EUframes_cy.csv`, 270 country-years | fixed effects for country and year, conventional standard errors | t = −3.804 on 233 df |
| KQXUE | `analyst_KQXUE.csv`, 270 country-years | a fixed effect for each country, conventional standard errors | t = −7.169 on 242 df |
| 018OL | `analyst_018OL.csv`, 420 cells of country, year and wave | random intercepts for country, year and wave, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom | t = −1.206 on 396.9 df |

## 5. What a reproduction needs

**On the slides.** The slides explain why everyone with the same analyst got the same t. They then set out what a reproduction needs besides the code, the data and the right versions of both, and the slips that three of the five pipelines carry, with what each slip does to the t.

## 6. Hands-on 3b – Reading deposited code

[KQXUE, `task2.do`](https://osf.io/vycgd/){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [018OL, the R Markdown file of Task 2](https://osf.io/nz7ka/){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [C6HJR, the folder of April 2025](https://osf.io/6zqct/){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Open the OSF deposit of the analyst whom you reproduced, find the line that carries the slip, and write one check that would have caught it, as a sentence or as a line of R. Before the break, copy your Task 3 cell and its output into your notes if you work in the browser lab, because the page forgets everything when it reloads.

**By the end of the part** you can describe how the panel was built and where its slips could hide, you have run the checks that find such slips, and you have reproduced a recorded result to the third decimal.
